subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
subtype: Approach: deciding a personal rule for what counts as own work [Thinking]
passage: Irfan pulled up the school's technology policy on the laptop before dinner and read the paragraph on AI twice. Explaining ideas: allowed. Graded work: must be your own. That part was clear. Now for his own rule. He wrote in his notebook: AI may explain a topic I don't get. AI may check an answer after I've written it. AI may not write anything I hand in. He thought about the history essay due Friday. If the tool wrote a paragraph, whose thinking would that be? Not his. If it explained the causes of the revolt and he wrote them in his own words, that was his. Wasim texted: just let it write the intro, nobody checks. Irfan replied: I know. I'd know. He closed the chat and started the outline.

qa.a: Irfan read the paragraph on AI in the school's technology policy twice.

qa.q: How does Irfan seem to feel about Wasim's suggestion?
qa.a: Irfan seems resolute and self-respecting, since he calmly answers I'd know and starts the outline.

qa.q: What could Irfan do if he gets stuck on the essay?
qa.a: Irfan could ask the tool to explain the causes in simpler words, or ask the teacher what is allowed, then write it himself.

qa.q: How might Wasim see Irfan's rule?
qa.a: Wasim may find it strict, since nobody checks, but may also feel a nudge to think about his own use.

grounding: A student decides AI may explain ideas and check his work but written answers must be his own, and reads the school policy to confirm the line.

passage:
"Shankar, you've had that AI tab open all evening. Is it writing your history project?"
"No, Shreya Didi. That's the whole point. I'm deciding what it's allowed to do."
"Allowed?"
"For me. Explaining things is fine. Like, I asked it why the Non-Cooperation Movement was called off, and it explained it simpler than the book."
"And the project?"
"The project I write. Every sentence. If it gets marks, it's mine."
"What about checking?"
"It can check my maths steps after I finish. Not before."
"Who made these rules, you?"
"Me first. Then I read the school's policy page to see if I'm right." He scrolled. "Here. 'AI may be used to understand concepts; submitted work must be the student's own unless the teacher says otherwise.' So I'm inside the line."
"Hmm. Write that on a sticky note for your screen."
"Already did."

qa.q: What did Shankar ask the AI about?
qa.a: Why the Non-Cooperation Movement was called off.

qa.q: How does Shankar feel about where the line is?
qa.a: Shankar feels confident and a little proud, having worked out a rule first and then found it fits the school's policy.

qa.q: What else could Shankar do if one teacher's rule differs for an assignment?
qa.a: He could ask that teacher before starting and follow their rule for that task, since the policy lets teachers say otherwise.

qa.q: How might Shreya see Shankar's rule?
qa.a: Shreya starts off suspicious that the AI is writing the project, but ends up approving and suggesting a sticky note to keep the rule in view.

grounding: Shows a student deciding that AI may explain and check but graded answers must be his own, then reading the school policy to confirm the line.

subtopic: Using AI tools for learning without cheating
subtype: Approach: deciding a personal rule for what counts as own work [Thinking]
passage: Last year, when our school first allowed AI tools in the computer lab, I had no idea where the line was. I'm Naveen. My friend Anirban used it for everything, even his birthday wishes. I didn't want to be the only one doing things the slow way, but I also didn't want to hand in something I couldn't explain. So one evening I sat with my school diary and wrote a rule for myself: the AI can explain, quiz me, and check my work after I've done it. Anything with marks attached, I write myself. Then I found the policy printed at the back of the diary and read it twice. It said almost the same thing, plus one line I'd missed: tell the teacher if you used it. I added that. Looking back, having the rule written down meant I stopped arguing with myself every night.

qa.q: Where did Naveen find the school policy?
qa.a: It was printed at the back of the school diary.

qa.q: What was Naveen feeling before writing the rule?
qa.a: Naveen felt unsure and torn, not wanting to be the only slow one but uneasy about handing in work that couldn't be explained.

qa.q: What else could help Naveen keep to the rule?
qa.a: Naveen could keep a short note of how AI was used on each assignment, so it is easy to tell the teacher when needed.

qa.q: How might Anirban see Naveen's rule?
qa.a: Anirban, who uses AI for everything, might find the rule slow or strict at first, but it could also make him think about his own use.

grounding: Illustrates a student setting a personal rule on what counts as their own work with AI, then checking it against the school policy.
